doc: Value-dependent carrier claiming, shared by server/specs/ValueDependentClaiming.tla and the Rust test `value_dependent_claiming_instances` (server/crates/domain/src/rules/claiming_instances_tests.rs). Each instance is a set of message rules over the carriers `a`, `b` and `c`: a `read` takes the first present of its candidates (present mode) and emits a message where it parses; a `claim` reads the same way and emits nothing; a `compose` owns exactly the members that parse and emits where one does. `fallback` is a stage-fallback read, evaluated after the dialect rules with what they own. A span assigns every carrier `absent`, `bad` (does not parse) or `ok`, and holds a set of the rules' gates. Both checkers enumerate every span of every instance; `refused` instances are the ones the compiler must refuse (an earlier rule reading a member of a later compose, which would starve it), and `expect` lists hand-written answers both must reproduce. The Rust test realises carrier `x` as attribute `vdc.x` (`ok` is the JSON text "x" in quotes, `bad` is an unterminated object), and the gate of rule `r` as the attribute `vdc.gate.r`.

instances.doc: An alias read, a claim on its second spelling, and a later reader of that spelling.

expect.doc: A bad primary commits: r1 owns nothing and does not hand over to `b`; the claim takes `b`, so r3, whose first present candidate is `b`, is dropped and does not reach `c`, which the fallback then reads.
Both spellings readable: r1 owns its primary, the claim owns the alias, r3 loses.
A gate that does not hold reads nothing, so the later rule takes the carrier.

instances.doc: A compose ranked ahead of the readers of its members, as the compiler requires.

expect.doc: The compose owns only the member that parsed, so the bad one is left to nobody it could not read either; the fallback finds its carrier owned.
A compose whose gate fails owns nothing; the reader takes `b`.

instances.doc: A claim and a fallback reading the same carrier.

expect.doc: The claim emits nothing and still keeps the fallback off its carrier.

instances.doc: A reader ranked ahead of a compose that needs its carrier: refused, because the compose would be dropped whole wherever the reader took `a`.
Two composes sharing a member: the later one is starved by the earlier, so the pair is refused.
